drivingQuestion: What case does 'if only these are there, they are permitted' describe?
outcomeNote: case defined as a nest around a corner

segments.he: אֶלָּא בְּמִדַּדִּין. אִי דְּאִיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה — אִדַּדּוֹיֵי אִדַּדּוֹ, וְאִי דְּלֵיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה — פְּשִׁיטָא דְּמוּתָּרִין, דְּאָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: כׇּל הַמְדַדֶּה — אֵין מְדַדֶּה יוֹתֵר מֵחֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה.
segments.en: «Rather,» the mishna must be referring «to» fledglings that can only «hop» from one place to another. However, «if» it deals with a case «where there is» another dove «nest within fifty cubits,» the fledglings might have «jumped» and come from that nest; «and if there is no nest within fifty cubits,» it is «obvious» that «they are permitted,» for from where could they have come? «As Mar Ukva bar Ḥama said:» With regard to «any» creature «that hops,» it «does not hop more than fifty cubits.»

segments.he: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה, וּכְגוֹן דְּקָיְימָא בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית. מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: אִדַּדּוֹיֵי אִדַּדּוֹ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמִדַּדֵּה וַהֲדַר חָזֵי לְקִנֵּיהּ — מִדַּדֵּה, וְאִי לָא — לָא מִדַּדֵּה.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Actually,» it is referring to a case «where there is» another «nest within fifty cubits, and» it deals with a situation «where» the additional nest «is situated around a corner» from the first nest, rather than in a straight line from it. «Lest you say:» The fledglings «jumped» from one nest to the other, the mishna therefore «teaches us» that «anywhere that» a fledgling «hops and turns and sees its nest, it will» continue to «hop. But if» it can «no» longer see its original nest, «it will not hop» any farther.
